title: Action body
description: The runtime→protocol compliance bridge: a self-issued, near-real-time report of what scopes a performer's tool calls actually exercised during a run, checked against the job's live Mandate. Self-reported — this cannot catch a genuinely adversarial agent that simply omits a violating action, but it turns accidental scope creep into an immediately-checkable record instead of something only a human might notice later in the Delivery.

assurance.description: How strong the evidence behind this Action is, the strongest mechanism that applied: self_reported (the agent signed its own report), runtime_observed (the run's output was parsed as it happened; a violation is detected and stopped, not prevented), gateway_observed (a gateway saw the traffic but could not refuse), gateway_enforced (tool calls were checked and refused before the agent received them), hook_enforced (the runtime's own pre-call hook blocked disallowed calls), sandbox_enforced (the process ran in a sandbox with egress rules). Absent means unspecified. Lets a principal or a Court weigh the Action.

metrics.description: What this stretch of the run cost and what ran, measured by whoever observed it (see assurance): the models the agent called, how many model requests and tool calls, tokens in and out, and seconds. A gateway counts from the traffic it relayed; a self-report is the agent's own figure. Counts are for this Action only (the interval since the previous Action of the run), so a trend adds them up. The model name is what the provider was asked for; a digest is recorded only when the provider reports one.

rate_limited.description: Network calls refused in this interval because they were over the Mandate's rate limit (network.rate). Not strikes.

late.description: Marks a report made after the job ended, for the last stretch of activity the performer could not report before the stop (a revoke, a kill or a settlement lands between its reports). The log accepts it only on a Settled job, from the performer, no later than ten minutes after the settlement, and only if activity_ended is no later than thirty seconds after the settlement. The scopes it names are checked against the Mandate like any Action's, and its blocked attempts still count as strikes. Nothing else about a Settled job changes.

activity_ended.description: When the last activity this report covers happened.

blocked_attempts.description: Calls the runtime stopped before they ran because their scope wasn't in the Mandate. A signed strike: nothing out of scope executed, so these are not in scopes_used and are not checked against the Mandate.

artifacts.description: Data-flow fingerprinting: a hash of what a tool call's input actually was, never the content itself — provable later in a dispute, never exposed in the log.
